# Type Reference

An auto-generated catalogue of every entity, connection, and enum exported from `filament.types`. It is regenerated from the source whenever the types are, so it never drifts. For the concepts behind this catalogue — the base-class hierarchy, common fields, and naming conventions — see [Finding Entity & Connection Types](finding-types.md).

> Every entity also carries the common `EntityBase` fields (`id`, `created_at`, `created_by_id`, `updated_at`, `updated_by_id`, `scope_id`), and every connection additionally carries `from_id`, `to_id`, `from_entity`, and `to_entity`. Those are documented once in [Finding Types](finding-types.md#the-base-class-hierarchy) and are not repeated below.

### `ActualStatusEnum` (`Enum`)

Represents the status of an actual, reflecting the task's progress and readiness to proceed.

| Member | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `Waiting` | The task cannot yet start because its planned start date is in the future (tomorrow or later). |
| `NotReady` | The task cannot yet start because at least one first-level upstream dependency is not complete. |
| `ReadyToStart` | All first-level upstream dependencies are complete (or the task has no dependencies), but no work has started on the task yet. |
| `InProgress` | The task has started work, indicated by either an open time log or a qualifying submitted work time log. |
| `Complete` | The task's billing proportion has reached 1.0. |

### `DataProcessingStatus` (`Flag`)

Represents the status of data processing in the system.

| Member | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `Unknown` | Represents an undefined or uninitialized state of data processing. This status is used when the processing state is not explicitly set or is unknown. |
| `Pending` | Indicates that the data processing is queued but has not yet started. This status represents an initial stage where the processing is awaiting execution. |
| `Processing` | Indicates that data is currently undergoing processing. This status represents an active state where data processing operations are being performed. |
| `Complete` | Indicates that data processing has been completed successfully. This status signifies the final stage where all processing tasks are finished and the data is ready or has been fully processed. |
| `All` | Represents the combined state where all stages of data processing (Pending, Processing, and Complete) are included. This status signifies a scenario where every processing state is jointly applicable. |

| Member | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |

### `ErrorCodes` (`Enum`)

Represents a set of predefined error codes that can be used to indicate

| Member | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `None_` | Represents the absence of any error or issue. This is used as a default or initial state to indicate that no error condition is present. |
| `NotSupported` | Indicates that the operation or functionality being requested is not supported by the system or the current context. This error code typically arises when attempting to use a feature or perform an action that is not implemented or is intentionally restricted. |
| `InternalError` | Represents an internal error within the system. This error code indicates unexpected or unhandled conditions that occur within the application, often due to logic faults, resource issues, or framework-level problems. |
| `SerializationError` | Indicates an error related to serialization processes. This error code represents issues encountered during conversion of data to or from a serialized format, such as incorrect format, deserialization failures, or unsupported data structures. |
| `AuthenticationError` | Indicates an error related to authentication failures. This error code represents issues such as invalid credentials, expired authentication tokens, or incorrect authentication mechanisms. |
| `PermissionDenied` | Indicates that the requested operation or access was denied due to insufficient permissions. This error code is used to signify a lack of authorization or access rights for the current user or process. |
| `ScenarioError` | Represents an error related to the execution or processing of a specific scenario. This error code is used to identify issues that occur in scenario-based workflows or operations. |
| `SubscriptionError` | Indicates an error related to subscription handling or processes. This error code typically signifies issues such as subscription failures, unexpected subscription states, or invalid subscription operations. |
| `RequestError` | Indicates an error that occurs due to issues in processing a request. This error code is typically used when a client request cannot be completed as expected, often due to malformed requests, unexpected input, or service limitations. |
| `Cancelled` | Indicates that an operation was cancelled prior to completion. This error code is used when a process is explicitly interrupted or terminated by a user or system action. |
| `NotReady` | Indicates that the operation or resource is not in a state ready to proceed. This error code is used to signify that certain preconditions or preparations are incomplete or missing. |
| `NoData` | Indicates that no data is available for the requested operation or query. This error code can be used to signal situations where the system was unable to retrieve or find the required data. |
| `ConnectionError` | Represents an error condition that occurs during connection attempts or operations. This error code is used to indicate failures or issues related to establishing or maintaining a connection. |
| `TypeError` | Represents an error condition that occurs when there is a mismatch or invalid type detected. This error code is used to indicate issues arising from improper or unexpected type usage. |
| `RateLimitExceeded` | Indicates that the API key has exceeded its configured rate limit. This error code is used when too many requests have been made within the rate limit window. |

### `ScheduleSegmentModeEnum` (`Enum`)

Represents the mode of a schedule segment within the scheduling system.

| Member | Description |
| ------ | ----------- |
| `Unknown` | Represents an undefined or unknown mode for a schedule segment. This value is typically used as a default or placeholder when the mode of the segment is not explicitly set or cannot be determined. |
| `Work` | Represents a mode in which the schedule segment is allocated for performing work-related tasks. This mode is used to designate time periods where core operational activities are carried out. |
| `Buffer` | Represents a buffer mode for a schedule segment. This mode is used to allocate time specifically designated as a buffer or transitional period, separate from active work or processing segments. |
| `Processing` | Represents a mode where a schedule segment is designated for processing operations. This time is considered background processing, and is not assigned to a user. |
| `Group` | Represents a mode indicating a grouped or collective category for a schedule segment. This value is used when the segment is intended to encapsulate or represent multiple related segments or activities typically treated collectively. |
| `User` | Represents a user-defined mode for a schedule segment. This value allows customization or designation of a segment based on user-specific requirements or configurations within the scheduling system. |
| `Event` | Represents a schedule segment designated for events. This mode is used to allocate time specifically for events within the scheduling system. |
| `TimeLog` | Represents a schedule segment that corresponds to logged time. This mode is used to indicate time that has already been worked and recorded via a TimeLogEntity. |

## Services

Types grouped by backend service. Within each service, entities come first, then connections (where the service defines any). Types tagged _abstract base_ / _generic base_ are shared parents you don't use directly.

### Core

#### Entities

##### `ErrorEntity`

Represents an error that has occurred, including details such as message, error code, and stack trace.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `original_tenant_id` | `UUID` | — | Identifies the unique identifier of the tenant associated with the original source of the error. This property is used to trace the origin of the error in multi-tenant environments. |
| `message` | `str` | `''` | Describes the textual information associated with the error entity. Typically provides a human-readable description or details about the error. |
| `error_code` | `ErrorCodes` | `ErrorCodes.None_` | Represents the specific code that categorizes the type of error encountered. Used for defining error types in a structured and identifiable manner. |
| `stack_trace` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | Contains the stack trace information related to the error. Typically used for debugging purposes to trace the sequence of method calls that led to the error, providing insight into its origin and context. |

| `status` | `RequestStatus` | `RequestStatus.Unknown` | The status of the request. |
| `error_message` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | Error message if the request failed. |
| `affected_entities` | `list[str]` | — | List of affected entity IDs. |

### Actual Service

#### Entities

##### `ActualEntity`

Defines actual time and cost spent on a task and details of when it was started and finished.

_Extends:_ `ReferenceEntityBase`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `reference_type` | `str` | `''` | The entity type this references |
| `reference_id` | `UUID` | — | The id of the referenced entity |
| `reference` | `Optional[EntityBase]` | `None` | Represents a linked entity instance. |
| `duration_to_date` | `datetime.timedelta` | — | The total time duration worked on the task to date, derived from TimeLog schedule segments. |
| `duration_forecast_total` | `datetime.timedelta` | — | The total forecast duration for the task, derived from all qualifying schedule segments (Work and TimeLog). Represents the predicted total duration at task completion — the sum of planned remaining work and time already logged. |
| `processing_duration` | `datetime.timedelta` | — | The duration of additional automated processing associated with the task. Currently always zero; reserved for future use. |
| `cost_forecast_total` | `float` | `0` | The forecast cost in the organization's reference currency, derived from all qualifying schedule segments (Work and TimeLog) and compensation records for assigned users. |
| `cost_to_date` | `float` | `0` | The actual cost incurred to date in the organization's reference currency. |
| `chargeable_total` | `float` | `0` | The total chargeable amount for this actual in the organization's reference currency, converted at the current rate. For tasks this comes from `Chargeable`. For groups this is the sum of child chargeable totals. |
| `chargeable_to_date` | `float` | `0` | The chargeable amount earned to date, equal to `ChargeableTotal` multiplied by the billing proportion derived from time log ProportionComplete values. For groups this is the sum of child chargeable-to-date values. |
| `costs_by_currency_rate_id` | `dict[UUID, float]` | — | The monetary costs attributed to this task, keyed by CurrencyRateEntity ID. Each entry represents a cost amount at a specific currency rate. |
| `currency_id` | `UUID` | — | The resolved currency for this cost calculation. Determined from the organization's default currency. |
| `currency` | `Optional[CurrencyEntity]` | `None` | A helper property for setting the CurrencyId property. Pass in a CurrencyEntity type. |
| `start_instant` | `datetime.datetime` | — | The instant (UTC) when work on the task started. |
| `end_instant` | `datetime.datetime` | — | The instant (UTC) when work on the task finished. |
| `status` | `ActualStatusEnum` | `ActualStatusEnum.Waiting` | The computed status of this actual, derived from task progress and dependency state. For task actuals: Complete if logged work remains with no planned Work segments left, InProgress if work has started, NotReady if any first-level upstream dependency is incomplete, Waiting if the planned start date is tomorrow or later, otherwise ReadyToStart. For group actuals: rolled up from child statuses. Any child InProgress makes the group InProgress; all children Complete makes the group Complete; any partially complete child also makes the group InProgress; otherwise any ReadyToStart child makes the group ReadyToStart; otherwise any Waiting child makes the group Waiting, and empty or fully blocked groups remain Waiting/NotReady. |
| `office_location_ids` | `list[UUID]` | — | The deduplicated office location IDs associated with this actual. For tasks this comes from `TaskOfficeLocationConnection` rows. For groups this is the union of child office location IDs. |
| `warnings_data` | `Optional[str]` | `None` | JSON-serialized warnings for this actual, keyed by warning type with sets of affected user IDs as values. Null when there are no warnings. |

##### `ScheduleSegmentEntity`

Represents a segment in a schedule, including metadata such as name, description, time period, mode, and parent segment relationships.

_Extends:_ `ReferenceEntityBase`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `reference_type` | `str` | `''` | The entity type this references |
| `reference_id` | `UUID` | — | The id of the referenced entity |
| `reference` | `Optional[EntityBase]` | `None` | Represents a linked entity instance. |
| `name` | `str` | `''` | The name of the schedule segment. Represents a descriptive or identifying title for the segment. |
| `description` | `str` | `''` | A brief textual explanation or characterization of the schedule segment. Provides additional context or details about the segment. |
| `reasons_data` | `str` | `''` | A descriptive field that provides justification or explanation related to the schedule segment, stored as a serialized JSON string. |
| `start_instant` | `datetime.datetime` | — | Represents the starting point in time for the schedule segment as an instant. This property defines the exact timestamp from which the segment begins. |
| `end_instant` | `datetime.datetime` | — | The end time of the schedule segment, represented as an instant in time. Defines the point at which this segment concludes. |
| `user_type` | `str` | `''` | Specifies the type of user associated with the schedule segment. Represents a categorization or classification of the user, such as regular user, placeholder, etc. |
| `user_id` | `UUID` | — | Represents the unique identifier of the user associated with a schedule segment. This property is used to link the schedule segment to a specific user entity within the system. |
| `user` | `Optional[Union[PlaceholderUserEntity, UserEntity]]` | `None` | Represents an entity related to the schedule segment, associated via a user type and user identifier. Used to establish and manage a link to the corresponding user or entity providing context or ownership for the schedule segment. |
| `mode` | `ScheduleSegmentModeEnum` | `ScheduleSegmentModeEnum.Unknown` | The mode of the schedule segment, specifying its functional purpose within the schedule. Possible values include Unknown, Work, Buffer, Processing, Group, User, and Event. |
| `parent_ids` | `list[UUID]` | — | The identifier of the parent segments associated with the current schedule segment entity. Used to establish hierarchical relationships between segments. |
| `parents` | `Optional[list[ScheduleSegmentEntity]]` | `None` | The parent schedule segment entities. Represents the hierarchical relationship where this segment is a child of another segment. |
| `priority` | `float` | `1` | The priority of this schedule segment, derived from the associated task's priority. Meeting segments have a priority of 1.0. |
| `time_log_id` | `Optional[UUID]` | `None` | The identifier of the time log entry associated with this schedule segment. This is used to link logged work time segments back to their source time log. |
| `time_log` | `Optional[TimeLogEntity]` | `None` | The time log entry associated with this schedule segment. Used to conveniently link a segment to its source time log. |

_Extends:_ `TaskDependencyOverrideConnectionBase_2`

| Field | Type | Default | Description |

### User License Service

#### Entities

##### `UserLicenseEntity`

An hourly record of which users have held a given license type during the hour. One row

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| ----- | ---- | ------- | ----------- |
| `license_type` | `UserLicenseType` | `UserLicenseType.User` | The license type this snapshot is for. |
| `instant` | `datetime.datetime` | — | The hour bucket this snapshot represents, expressed as an `Instant` floored to the start of the UTC hour. |
| `user_ids` | `list[UUID]` | — | The set of user ids that have held this license type at any propagation during the hour represented by `Instant`. Updated by union — entries are never removed within the bucket. |
| `month_license_count` | `int` | `0` | A moment-in-time snapshot of license usage for this `LicenseType`, sealed at the last propagation of this hour bucket. Computed as max(dayMin, priorValue) where: dayMin is the minimum of UserIds.Count across every entity on the same UTC day for the same license type (including this one), as observed at the moment of this hour's last propagation. priorValue is the `MonthLicenseCount` of the latest-Instant entity in the same UTC calendar month strictly before today, for the same license type. Gap days (calendar days with no entities) are walked over — the chain runs back through prior days in the month until one with entities is found, stopping at the start of the month. priorValue is 0 only when today is the 1st of the month or no prior day in the current month has any entities. What this value is and is not: It resets at the start of each UTC calendar month — values do not carry across month boundaries. It is not strictly monotonic within a month: later hours of a day typically see a smaller dayMin as more rows accumulate, so an entity's MonthLicenseCount can be lower than another entity earlier on the same day. Two entities on the same day can therefore hold different values. Within an hour bucket it is sealed by that hour's last propagation; later hours never overwrite it. To read "the current month's value as of right now", look at the latest-Instant entity in the current calendar month for the license type — not "the maximum value seen in the month so far". They are not the same. |
